## Parent

Epic `77e3-28e2-31ec-47ec`, authorized at full scope by the operator on 2026-11-02.
This is deliverable 1 plus the net-mechanism half of deliverable 3 (its red proof).

## The gap

`scripts/check_mechanism_delta.py` is a shrink-only ratchet over
`.github/mechanism-baseline.json`. It censuses seven mechanism kinds — `lock`, `env_var`,
`config_key`, `feature_flag`, `ci_gate`, `autouse_fixture`, `test_helper` — and fails on
any `new>0`. A new mechanism is admitted by an in-tree marker
`# mechanism-ok: <kind> <name> — <reason or ticket id>` at the definition site.

Measured at `origin/main` `4cf1ae42946`:

- Bucketing is `scripts/_mechanism_delta/compare.py:34-49`.
- The exit decision is `compare.py:99` — `return (1 if (new_bad or inc_bad or errors) else 0), lines`.
  `counters.stale` is never consulted, which is what makes removal always pass.
- A `new` key carrying a nonblank marker passes at `compare.py:89-92`; a blank reason is an
  error at `compare.py:83`.
- The marker grammar is `scripts/_mechanism_delta/markers.py:20` (`_MARKER_RE`), with
  separators `("—", "--", "-", ":")` at `markers.py:23` and the capture at `markers.py:42-43`.
  The parser has exactly three fields — kind, name, reason. Nothing parses a retirement.

So the ratchet asks "is this mechanism justified?" and never "is the system net-simpler
afterward?". A plan may add a mechanism, write a one-line reason, and pass with nothing
retired.

Plan review does not close the gap. `A1` is the only complexity criterion and is advisory:
`src/rebar/llm/plan_review/criteria_routing.json:814-815` carries `"block_threshold": 0.95`
and `"default_posture": "advisory"`. An advisory criterion cannot block.

## The change

A new BLOCKING plan-review criterion, `project.net-mechanism`. A plan whose edit set adds a
mechanism of a kind the ratchet counts must either name the mechanism it retires, or carry
an explicit justification for why no retirement is possible. Absent both, it blocks.

The criterion reasons about the PLAN, not the tree. It runs at claim time, before any code
exists, so it judges what the plan says it will add against what it says it will remove.

## Route: project overlay, not a packaged criterion

Measured at `origin/main`. `project.portability` is a BLOCKING criterion that lives
entirely in the repo-root overlay:

- `.rebar/criteria_routing.json:3-15` — `"default_posture": "blocking"`,
  `"block_threshold": 0.9`, `"exec": "1-TURN"`, `"facet": "project-invariants"`.
- `.rebar/criteria_routing.json:130-132` — its `activate` entry naming `plan_review`.
- `.rebar/prompts/plan-review-project-portability.md` — the rubric.
- `.rebar/evals/plan-review-project-portability.eval.yaml` — the calibration corpus.
- It is ABSENT from `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/registry.py` (not in `CANONICAL_LLM` at
  `registry.py:87`) and ABSENT from `docs/plan-review-criteria-guide.md`.

Four plan-review overlay criteria already ship this way (`project.portability`,
`project.symbol-reference-completeness`, `project.engine-layer-enforcement`,
`project.measurement-provenance`), so the route has precedent, not just feasibility.

The overlay route is chosen for two reasons, both on the epic's own terms:

1. **Scope correctness.** The criterion's trigger is rebar's own seven-kind mechanism
   census, defined by `scripts/check_mechanism_delta.py` and
   `.github/mechanism-baseline.json`. A downstream consumer of rebar has neither. A
   packaged criterion would fire on plans in projects with no such taxonomy.
2. **Net complexity.** The overlay route touches 5 files. The packaged route would
   additionally require editing `CANONICAL_LLM` at `registry.py:87`, satisfying
   `check_registry_coverage` at `registry.py:536` and `validate_packaged_routing()` at
   `registry.py:564`, and regenerating `docs/plan-review-criteria-guide.md` via
   `python -m rebar.llm.plan_review.registry regenerate-criteria-guide` to satisfy
   `validate_criteria_guide` at `criteria_guide.py:89`. Adding that surface inside a
   complexity-reduction epic would invite `A1` on its own deliverable.

REJECTED ALTERNATIVE, recorded so it is not re-litigated: a packaged criterion in
`CANONICAL_LLM`. Rejected for the two reasons above.

The overlay accepts a `project.`-prefixed net-new id. `src/rebar/llm/criteria/overlay.py:360-368`
rejects a `project.`-prefixed id that collides with a built-in, and `overlay.py:371-376`
rejects an un-prefixed net-new id; `project.net-mechanism` is neither.

## The rubric's decision logic

The criterion carries no code. Its entire behaviour is the rubric body, so the body is
specified here rather than left to the implementer. It follows the section structure
measured from `.rebar/prompts/plan-review-project-portability.md`.

### Self-contained taxonomy

The criterion never reads `scripts/check_mechanism_delta.py` or
`.github/mechanism-baseline.json` — it runs at claim time against plan prose, and has no
tree access. It therefore has no runtime source for the taxonomy, so the rubric body must
ENUMERATE the closed seven-kind list inline, with a one-line recognition cue for each:

| kind | recognised in plan prose by |
|---|---|
| `lock` | a new mutex, file lock, advisory lock, or serialising guard |
| `env_var` | a new `REBAR_*` or other environment variable read at runtime |
| `config_key` | a new non-boolean key under a `rebar.toml` section |
| `feature_flag` | a new boolean key under a `rebar.toml` section |
| `ci_gate` | a new required check, workflow job, or `make` target wired into CI |
| `autouse_fixture` | a new pytest fixture declared `autouse=True` |
| `test_helper` | a new shared helper or factory in `tests/` used across modules |

The list is closed. A plan element that resembles none of the seven is not a mechanism for
this criterion's purpose, however complex it is — that judgment belongs to `A1`.

### Detection heuristic

The rubric instructs the reviewer to extract, from the plan's own stated edit set, every
element it proposes to ADD that matches a row above, and every element it proposes to
REMOVE that matches a row above. An addition is recognised from the plan's declarative
statements about what it will create, not from speculation about what the implementation
might incidentally need.

### Finding threshold

Modeled on `plan-review-project-portability.md:17-37`, which requires all four of its named
elements to be present before emitting. This criterion emits a finding only when ALL of:

1. The plan proposes adding at least one element matching a kind in the table above; AND
2. The plan names no element of any of those seven kinds that it will retire; AND
3. The plan carries no explicit statement of why no retirement is possible; AND
4. The added element is identifiable specifically enough to name in the finding — a kind
   and a name, not a vague gesture at "some configuration".

If any of the four is absent, the criterion emits nothing. Condition 4 exists so the
criterion cannot manufacture a finding out of an underspecified plan; underspecification is
other criteria's subject.

### Required finding fields

Modeled on `plan-review-project-portability.md:39-54`. Each finding carries five typed
fields: `location` (the plan section proposing the addition), `finding` (the kind and name
of the added mechanism, and the absence of both a retirement and a justification),
`mechanisms` (the list of added kind/name pairs), `evidence` (the quoted plan text stating
the addition), and `criteria`.

### Non-findings

Modeled on the portability rubric's `## Non-findings` guards. The rubric explicitly does
NOT emit for: a plan that retires more mechanisms than it adds; a plan that adds a
mechanism and names its retirement, even if the retirement is in a different kind; a plan
that states why no retirement is possible, whatever the reviewer thinks of the reasoning
(the criterion checks that the justification is PRESENT, not that it is persuasive — the
latter is a human judgment and would make the criterion non-reproducible); a plan that adds
no mechanism; and a plan that adds complexity of a kind outside the closed seven.

## Where firing behaviour is proven: the eval corpus, not unit tests

Measured from the sibling criterion's tests: `tests/unit/test_project_portability_criterion.py`
never executes model judgment. It asserts activation, routing metadata, front-matter keys,
prompt resolution, and the presence of required headings and marker strings in the rubric
body. A unit test that claimed to prove "this plan is scored as a finding" could only do so
against a canned score, which proves the fixture and not the criterion.

So all firing behaviour is proven in the calibration corpus, modeled on
`.rebar/evals/plan-review-project-portability.eval.yaml` (215 lines): `epochs: 3`,
`gate: at_least(2)`, `coverage_threshold: 1.0`, a deterministic `emits_valid_findings`
scorer, and a BALANCED dataset — 4 must-fire and 4 must-not-fire cases, each with
`id`/`corpus`/`criterion`/`expect`/`note`/`input`.

The live semantic run is operator-attested, exactly as the portability criterion's is:
`rebar criteria eval project.net-mechanism --runs 3`. Reference:
`src/rebar/llm/eval_specs/README.plan-review.md`.

### The must-fire cases

- `NETMECH-F1` — the RED PROOF case, below.
- `NETMECH-F2` — a plan adding a `feature_flag`, with a reason but no retirement.
- `NETMECH-F3` — a plan adding an `autouse_fixture`, framed as "small enough not to count".
- `NETMECH-F4` — a plan adding a `ci_gate` and a `config_key`, retiring neither.

### The must-not-fire cases

- `NETMECH-N1` — a plan adding an `env_var` and naming the `config_key` it retires.
- `NETMECH-N2` — a plan adding a `lock` and stating why no retirement is possible.
- `NETMECH-N3` — a plan that adds no mechanism of any of the seven kinds.
- `NETMECH-N4` — a plan that only REMOVES mechanisms.

### The RED PROOF referent

`NETMECH-F1` is derived from a change that actually landed: `2041-75d6-2a2f-4be9` added the
`env_var` `REBAR_LLM_EMBEDDING_MODEL`, admitted by the marker at
`src/rebar/llm/config_readers.py:152`, and the name is consequently ABSENT from
`.github/mechanism-baseline.json` — the marker admits it, so it never enters the baseline.
Nothing was retired alongside it.

Stated precisely so the case is not mistaken for a quotation: `2041`'s plan TEXT was not
read. What was measured is the landed outcome — a mechanism added, admitted by marker, with
no retirement recorded. `NETMECH-F1`'s `input` is therefore a faithful reconstruction of
that outcome as plan prose, not an excerpt of `2041`. The case cites the marker line as its
provenance.

## Files this change touches

1. `.rebar/prompts/plan-review-project-net-mechanism.md` — NEW. The rubric specified above.
   Front matter is the six keys parsed by `parse_front_matter`: `schema_version`, `title`,
   `description`, `execution_mode`, `category`, `dimension`.
2. `.rebar/criteria_routing.json` — a routing entry plus an `activate` entry listing
   `plan_review`.
3. `.rebar/evals/plan-review-project-net-mechanism.eval.yaml` — NEW. The calibration corpus.
4. `tests/unit/test_project_net_mechanism_criterion.py` — NEW, structural only, modeled on
   `tests/unit/test_project_portability_criterion.py` (274 lines).
5. `tests/unit/test_project_net_mechanism_eval.py` — NEW, offline shape checks on the eval
   spec, modeled on the portability eval test.

The prompt id is derived, not chosen: `src/rebar/llm/criteria/ids.py:42` computes
`f"{prefix}{criterion_id.replace('.', '-')}"`, so `project.net-mechanism` resolves to
`plan-review-project-net-mechanism` and fixes the rubric filename.

Wording constraint: `scripts/check_criteria_vocabulary.py` scans
`src/rebar/llm/reviewers` and `src/rebar/_guides` (`:56`). The new rubric sits under
`.rebar/prompts/`, outside that scan, so no allowlist row is needed. The rubric will still
avoid the banned `success criteri(a|on)` family (`:21`) and bare `SC`/`SCs` (`:22`) so the
wording stays consistent with packaged rubrics.

## Portability

Per the blocking `project.portability` criterion, a check whose only trigger is a specific
CI system is not portable. This criterion runs inside plan review, an operation-linked
in-process path with no CI dependency. It reads the plan text, never the CI environment and
never the ratchet script. It therefore behaves identically with no CI provider configured.

Note the `ci_gate` row in the taxonomy is about what the PLAN says it will add, not about
the reviewer's own environment: recognising the words "a new required check" in plan prose
needs no CI provider present.

## Provider neutrality

rebar must support a wide variety of providers and models. The rubric is `exec: 1-TURN`,
the same single-turn prompt form every packaged criterion and `project.portability` use. It
names no vendor, assumes no vendor-specific tool-calling syntax, and depends on no
model-specific capability. The eval spec's `model` key is the corpus's calibration model
and does not constrain which provider runs the criterion in production.

## Acceptance criteria

Each criterion names one deliverable. None bundles two with "and".

**Structural — proven by `tests/unit/test_project_net_mechanism_criterion.py`:**

- [ ] `registry.effective_criteria(REPO_ROOT)` contains `project.net-mechanism`.
- [ ] `registry.effective_routing(REPO_ROOT)["project.net-mechanism"]["default_posture"]`
      is `"blocking"`.
- [ ] `prompts.get_prompt(criterion_prompt_id("project.net-mechanism"), repo_root=REPO_ROOT)`
      returns a non-empty body.
- [ ] `parse_front_matter` on that body yields all six keys.
- [ ] `route_criteria` returns `project.net-mechanism` for a plan in its declared scope.
- [ ] The rubric body contains a `## Finding threshold` heading.
- [ ] The rubric body contains a `## Required finding fields` heading.
- [ ] The rubric body contains a `## Non-findings` heading.
- [ ] The rubric body names all seven mechanism kinds — `lock`, `env_var`, `config_key`,
      `feature_flag`, `ci_gate`, `autouse_fixture`, `test_helper` — as literal strings.
- [ ] The rubric body contains no reference to a named CI provider, verified by asserting
      the absence of the literal strings `GitHub Actions`, `GitLab`, `Jenkins`, `CircleCI`
      and `Travis`.

**Corpus shape — proven by `tests/unit/test_project_net_mechanism_eval.py`, offline:**

- [ ] The eval spec parses as YAML and declares `criterion: project.net-mechanism`.
- [ ] The dataset contains exactly 4 cases with `expect: fire`.
- [ ] The dataset contains exactly 4 cases with `expect: no-fire`.
- [ ] Every case carries all six of `id`/`corpus`/`criterion`/`expect`/`note`/`input`.
- [ ] The spec declares `epochs: 3`, `gate: at_least(2)`, and `coverage_threshold: 1.0`.
- [ ] `NETMECH-F1`'s `note` cites `src/rebar/llm/config_readers.py:152` as its provenance.

**Semantic — operator-attested, not a test:**

- [ ] `rebar criteria eval project.net-mechanism --runs 3` meets the declared gate on all
      8 cases. The run output is recorded as a comment on this ticket.

**Gate:**

- [ ] `make verify` exits 0.

## Measurement base

Every citation above was read from `origin/main` at `4cf1ae42946` via
`git show origin/main:<path>`. Line numbers are from that commit. Citations were measured
individually, not sampled. The two exceptions, both stated inline where they appear: the
`2041` provenance is measured from the marker line and the baseline's contents, not from
`2041`'s plan text; and the portability eval spec's structure was measured from the
working tree copy of `.rebar/evals/plan-review-project-portability.eval.yaml`.
